plugin.name: AI Bridge
plugin.description:
Bring Claude Code into your JetBrains IDE for everyday development. Explore your codebase, plan changes and review proposed edits from the same workspace where you write code.

Features

  • Work with project context. Send selected code or the current file to a conversation with Alt+K, and preview the context before submitting a message.
  • Review changes in the IDE. Inspect proposed edits in the native diff viewer and open related files and terminals directly.
  • Organize your work. Use separate chat tabs, task templates and project queues. Reorder pending messages or combine them while the current task continues.
  • Keep useful conversations. Search past messages, save bookmarks and record decision notes.
  • Find your own messages. Your messages are tinted in a color you choose, and a column of dots at the edge of the chat jumps to each one.
  • Recover from dropped connections. Temporary network and server errors are retried automatically, and the reply continues where it stopped.
  • Control long-running tasks. Set project concurrency limits, monitor local CPU and memory usage, and reduce background rendering with low resource mode.
  • Choose how Claude works. Select the model and reasoning effort, schedule messages and configure automatic continuation after usage limits.
  • Use your preferred language. The interface includes English and Turkish.

Requirements and setup

Use a JetBrains IDE based on IntelliJ Platform 2023.1 or newer with a JCEF-enabled runtime, Node.js and an installed, configured Claude Code CLI. Open the plugin from the Tools menu or press Ctrl+Shift+C to start a conversation.

Use your existing Claude Code authentication or provider configuration. Messages, code context and tool requests are processed through the provider and services you configure; their usage terms and charges apply.

About

Independently maintained by Birkan Kader. Claude and Claude Code are Anthropic products. This plugin is not an official Anthropic or JetBrains product.

plugin.change-notes:
0.3 (2026-10-16)

  • DeepSeek Harness from a source checkout (Location set to the deepseek-harness folder) now starts in your project the same way pnpm dsh does in the checkout, without building it first. Before, it stopped with exit code 1 because its packages were looked up as built files.
  • When a harness stops, the chat shows the error it printed instead of only the last lines of its stack trace.

0.2 (2026-10-16)

  • Commits the agent makes no longer get a Co-Authored-By trailer. If your own Claude settings set attribution or includeCoAuthoredBy, that choice still applies.
  • Settings, Connection lists every agent harness (Claude Code, OpenCode, DeepSeek Harness) with its status, version and location. A missing harness installs with one click, and each one takes a Location: an executable, an npm install folder or a deepseek-harness source checkout.
  • A harness that is not on PATH is still found: AI Bridge checks its Location, then its own install, then PATH.
  • When a harness cannot start, the chat says why (command not found, or the exit code and error output) instead of "The agent closed its output".
  • The chat header, message author and input placeholder show the harness the chat runs on instead of always "Claude".

0.1 - AI Bridge (2026-10-16)

  • AI Bridge is now its own plugin (ID com.birkankader.ai-bridge) and its versions start again at 0.1. Builds up to 0.39 used a different ID and do not update to it: install AI Bridge from https://birkankader.com/plugins/ai-bridge/updatePlugins.xml, then uninstall the previous build so the two do not run side by side.
  • On first start, settings, saved accounts, harness conversations, project settings and custom chat titles are copied from the previous build. Its own files are left untouched.
  • New: choose OpenCode or DeepSeek Harness as the agent for new chats (Settings, Model, Agent harness). Both run through their official ACP command and are installed separately.
  • Experimental: computer use (Settings, General), off by default. The agent gets screenshot, mouse and keyboard tools from a local MCP server; in the default mode every action asks for permission.
  • The panel no longer looks blurry or pixelated after switching tabs, restoring a minimized window or moving it to a display with a different scale.
  • Windows: Bash tool output uses UTF-8 in IDE installs as well, so non-ASCII characters are no longer garbled.
  • Interface languages: Korean, Chinese and Japanese were removed; nine languages remain.
